papers.title: Retracts of well-filtered co-sober spaces are co-sober
papers.abstract: Xu and Zhao asked whether co-sobriety is inherited by the image of a continuous kernel operator, and more generally whether it is inherited by retracts. Both questions have recently been answered in the negative by Xu, Xu, Ji and Qiu. We prove that both questions have positive answers whenever the ambient space is, in addition, well-filtered; in particular they hold for every sober co-sober space. It follows that the ambient space of any counterexample to either question, such as that of Xu, Xu, Ji and Qiu, must be co-sober and not well-filtered. We give an example of a kernel-operator image that is not a direct instance of the inheritance results of Wen and Xu, and we identify the step of the argument that uses well-filteredness.

papers.title: Filters as a localization of nets
papers.abstract: Based on different notions of subnet in the literature, we define categories of nets and investigate their categorical relationships. We show that the category of proper filters with filter-preserving functions is, up to equivalence, a localization of four of these categories.

papers.title: Strongly meet continuous posets
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to introduce and investigate strongly meet continuous posets. It is shown that a poset is strongly meet continuous if and only if the Scott closure of the set of elements way below each element coincides with its principal ideal. Moreover, the Scott topology of every strongly meet continuous poset is shown to have a basis consisting of Scott open filters, and a countable strongly meet continuous dcpo that is not continuous is constructed. For posets with the one step closure property, strongly meet continuity is equivalent to continuity. Further, a poset is continuous if and only if it is strongly meet continuous and its Scott space is core compact. As a consequence, every core compact strongly meet continuous dcpo has a sober Scott space.

papers.title: Compactness-like properties in Alexandroff paratopological groups
papers.abstract: We study compactness-like and covering properties in non-compact Alexandroff paratopological groups. Several properties are characterized in terms of the order structure associated with the Alexandroff topology and the number of connected components. We establish equivalences among $2$-pseudocompactness, countable $o$-compactness, Baire, and an intersection property for increasing chains. We also obtain a common characterization of $\sigma$-local compactness, $\sigma$-compactness, the Lindel\"of property, and left $\omega$-precompactness in terms of the existence of a countable cofinal subset. Moreover, we characterize pseudocompactness, $H$-compactness, star-compactness, the countable chain condition, and the weakly Lindel\"of property by means of the number of connected components. Finally, we determine further implications among the properties considered and provide examples and counterexamples.

papers.title: Extremely amenable automorphism groups of countable structures
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the isomorphism relation of extremely amenable non-Archimedean Polish groups from the point of view of descriptive set theory. Our main result is that this relation is more complex than any isomorphism relation of countable structures in the Borel reducibility hierarchy.

papers.title: Metric-Measure Concentration and Strong Cosmic Censorship in Vacuum Gowdy Spacetimes
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth vacuum $T^3$-Gowdy maximal globally hyperbolic development is $C^2$-inextendible if its asymptotic velocity differs from one on a dense subset of the singular circle. This is the implication posed in Section~14.2 of Ringstr\"om's 2010 review. The proof compares the spacetime volume of a timelike boundary collar with that of a shrinking angular cone, using Killing transport and the Einstein constraint. We connect this criterion to Gromov's observable distance: the physical spatial mm-spaces satisfy the lower bound $d_{\rm conc}(X_\tau,*)\ge L(\tau)/(4+L(\tau))$, where $L(\tau)$ is the length of the orbit circle. If $L(\tau)\to0$, then $v_\infty\ge1$ everywhere, the critical set $\{v_\infty=1\}$ has Lebesgue measure zero, and the development is $C^2$-inextendible. Thus physical point concentration is sufficient for inextendibility, but is not necessary. We also give explicit, non-perturbative subcritical characteristic conditions on vacuum Cauchy data ensuring quantitative Kretschmann blow-up without using Gowdy asymptotic theorems in the curvature estimate. The exact volume-transfer identity yields predictive monotonicity criteria and distinguishes coordinate localization from intrinsic metric collapse. In the transversely expanding regime, observable rescalings with an extended transverse-length limit are classified as a point, a measured circle, or the maximal pyramid; a uniform spectral estimate eliminates all nontrivial toroidal Fourier sectors, including in the presence of spikes. The geometric framework is completed by quantitative tube estimates, a local CMC redistribution theorem, and constrained variational descriptions of the reduced energy current and normalized-volume flow.

papers.title: On the Variety of Hyperspace Selections
papers.abstract: If $f$ is a continuous selection for the Vietoris hyperspace $\mathcal{F}(X)$ of the nonempty closed subsets of a space $X$, then the point $p=f(X)\in X$ is not as arbitrary as it might seem at first glance. In fact, the set $\mathcal{O}_{cs}(X)$ of all these points reveals certain information about the variety of Vietoris continuous selections for $\mathcal{F}(X)$. Thus, for a connected space $X$, we will show that every point $p\in \mathcal{O}_{cs}(X)$ is not only noncut, but also an endpoint of $X$. Another result of this paper is that in an arbitrary topological space $X$, the closure of the set $\mathcal{O}_{cs}(X)$ is always a totally disconnected subset. Furthermore, we will also show that $\mathcal{O}_{cs}(X)$ is a closed subset of every first countable totally disconnected space $X$.

papers.title: Separately continuous maps into regular spaces and continuity of operations in separable semitopological groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every regular separable feebly compact semitopological group is a topological group. This answers a question of M. Tkachenko (2014) and extends the separable case of the author's 1994 theorem on Tychonoff pseudocompact groups to regular spaces. The proof rests on a new result: if $X$ is a separable Baire space, $Y$ is feebly compact and $Z$ is regular, then every separately continuous map $X\times Y\to Z$ is strongly quasicontinuous. Previously this was known only when $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ are Tychonoff. Using topological games of Banach-Mazur type, we extend the group theorem to regular separable Baire groups from a wider class of spaces, which contains all $p$-spaces, all feebly compact spaces and all products of a $p$-space with a feebly compact space. We also obtain local versions: the theorem holds for locally separable, locally feebly compact groups.

papers.title: Power topologies and uniformities on bistochastic operators
papers.abstract: We prove that the set of invertible Koopman operators attached to the usual interval probability space is dense (and hence dense $G_{\delta}$) in the space of bistochastic operators in the polynomial weak topology. This extends the non-polynomial analogue (due to Brown / Vershik / Ryzhikov / Eisner). We also show that the plain and polynomial weak topologies are distinct on bistochastic operators, confirming the distinction between the two results. Furthermore, the power topologies on the space of bistochastic operators recording weak convergence in powers up to $k+1$, $k\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ are all distinct, as are the analogous power uniformities on the automorphism group of the standard non-atomic Lebesgue probability measure.
